result.summary: The page layout is largely coherent, but several text-clipping and consistency defects are visible: the featured restaurant name collides with its rating, carousel card labels are cut off without ellipsis, the category chip row is clipped mid-chip, and favorite-button styling is inconsistent between cards.

issues.description: The 'Popular right now' restaurant title 'Tokumaru Ramen' is hard-clipped ('Ramer') where it meets the '4.8 (500+)' rating block on the same row, with no ellipsis or spacing.
issues.suggestion: Give the title a flex:1 with min-width:0 and text-overflow:ellipsis, and reserve fixed width for the rating so they never overlap.

issues.description: In the 'Fastest near you' carousel the third card's name ('Trattoria Piccol...') and its delivery fee are sliced off by the viewport edge without truncation, making it look broken rather than scrollable.
issues.suggestion: Add horizontal padding/peek so the next card is clearly a partial preview, and truncate card titles with ellipsis instead of hard clipping.

issues.description: The category filter chip row is cut mid-chip at the right edge with no visible indication that it scrolls or fades.
issues.suggestion: Add a gradient fade mask or a chevron/scroll affordance, and align chip clipping so partially shown chips read as intentional.

issues.description: The favorite (heart) buttons are styled inconsistently — white circular background on the ramen card versus a dark/transparent circle on the pizza card.
issues.suggestion: Use a single shared component with the same background, border and icon colour for all favorite buttons.

issues.description: The bottom pizza card is cut by the fixed bottom navigation bar, hiding its name, rating and delivery info with no visible scroll padding.
issues.suggestion: Add bottom padding equal to the nav bar height to the scroll container so the last card can be fully revealed.

issues.description: Cards in 'Fastest near you' show delivery time and fee but no rating, while the 'Popular right now' cards do, creating inconsistent information density.
issues.suggestion: Standardise the metadata shown on restaurant cards (rating, ETA, fee) across all sections.
